about:
# DadMode

![DadMode logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JonasBogvad/DadMode/main/media/logo.png)

A World of Warcraft: Forever addon for a player who keeps losing the party.
One addon, two roles: the person who gets lost ("dad") and the people who look after him ("guides").

Version 1.25.0. Game interface 16001 (WoW Forever 1.60).

## Install

1. Unzip. You get a folder called `DadMode`. Inside are `DadMode.toc`, 27 `.lua` files, `Arrow.tga`, `Logo.tga` and `README.md`.
   - **Downloaded from GitHub with Code, Download ZIP?** Then the folder is called `DadMode-main`. Rename it to `DadMode`, or the game will not load it. The zip under Releases has the right name already.
   - **Downloaded from GitHub with Code, Download ZIP?** Then the folder is called `DadMode-main`. Rename it to `DadMode`, or the game will not load it.
2. Put the folder in `World of Warcraft\_forever_\Interface\AddOns\`.
3. Fully close WoW and start it again. A new addon is not picked up by /reload.
4. On the character screen, click AddOns and check that DadMode is ticked.

## For dad

Nothing to set up except picking people once.

- The very first time you are in a party, a small window asks **Who do you want to find?** Click the names. Gold means picked. Press Done. It only opens by itself that one time. After that, click the gold arrow on the minimap to open it.
- Each picked person gets a **big arrow** at the top of the screen, with their name and the distance.
  - Green: close. Yellow: a bit away. Red: far.
  - Walk in the direction the arrow points.
- If you drift more than 110 yards from a picked person you see **You are far from **. A soft sound plays **once**, with the text. Then nothing more until you have been near again.
- If that person is far away **and in another zone**, there is no warning at all. They are doing something else on purpose. The arrow turns grey and says where they are: **in Orgrimmar**. Back in the same zone, everything is as before. A call still reaches you wherever they are.
- If someone calls you, you hear a sound, see their name in big text, and their arrow turns **white and pulses**. Walk to it.

The one rule: **white pulsing arrow and a beep means someone is calling you. Walk to the arrow.**

The text goes away after 10 seconds. The arrow keeps pulsing until you reach the person, for up to a minute. When you get there you see **You found **. To clear a call yourself, **click the big text**.

**The green FOLLOW button.** Under the arrows there is a big green button, like **FOLLOW Anna**. Click it and your character walks after that person by itself. It follows the first person you picked. While someone is calling you, it follows the caller and **flashes white** with the text **CLICK TO FOLLOW **. Following stops when you press a movement key, and the person has to be fairly close for it to start.

The button only flashes when the caller is close enough to be followed, about 30 yards. If the caller is further away or in another zone it stays calm, and the call text on screen says how many yards away the caller is. In a dungeon, where the game gives no distances, it flashes when the caller is in sight.

**Who may guide you.** Nobody can see how you are doing or call you until you have said yes to them.

The first time somebody tries to guide you (calls you, opens the window about you, sets a waypoint), a box appears: **Anna Stormhoof wants to be your guide. Yes / No**.

- **Yes**: that person is your guide from now on, and is picked for an arrow as well. You are not asked again.
- **No**: nothing from that person reaches you, and you are not asked about them again.

Until you answer, nothing of yours is sent to that person. Their window says you have not approved them yet.

**What your guides may see and do.** Everything is allowed for an approved guide unless you switch it off. Esc, Options, AddOns, DadMode, **My guides** (or `/dadmode guides`):

| Switch | Off means |
|---|---|
| See my level, zone and bag space | No status card for guides |
| See my gold | The gold is left out, the rest stays |
| See my quests | No quest list, no missing or dungeon check |
| See my gear and what is in my bags | No gear tab, no item comparison |
| Call me | Calls from guides do not show |
| Set waypoints for me | Waypoints are not taken |
| Tell me to put on gear | The gold button never appears |
| See my talents and point at one | The Talents tab says he does not share them, and nobody can point at a talent |

The switches are the same for all your guides. The same page lists everyone you approved or refused, with **Remove** and **Forget**. A removed or forgotten person is asked about again next time.

If you used DadMode before version 1.22, the people you had already picked are approved by themselves the first time they do something, so nothing changes for you.

**Settings.** All settings are on one page inside the game's own options: press **Esc**, then **Options**, then **AddOns** on the left, then **DadMode**. Three shortcuts go to the same page: the **Settings** button in the small DadMode window, a right click on the minimap button, and `/dadmode settings`. Each line has one button. Click it to switch to the next choice:

| Line | Choices |
|---|---|
| Who uses this computer | Someone being guided, or a guide |
| Show calls from the party on my screen | On, Off |
| Sound when someone calls | Soft ding, Map ping, Bell, Ready check, Horn (loud), No sound. Each click plays the sound |
| Sound when I drift far away | The same six |
| Far-away warning | On, Off |
| Green follow button | Shown, Hidden |
| Arrow size | Small, Medium, Large |
| Window size | 80%, 90%, 100%, 110%, 125%. Makes every DadMode window and bar smaller or bigger |
| Guide bar layout | 2 columns, 1 column |
| Try it: show a call on my own screen | Shows what dad sees: sound, text, and the pulsing arrow |
| Reset window sizes | Puts every window back to the size it came with |
| Arrows and follow button | Locked, or Unlocked so they can be dragged to a new spot |
| Compare drops with their gear | On, Off. Guides only. Covers item tooltips and the chat line on drops |
| My guides and what they may see | Opens the My guides page |
| Minimap button | Shown, Hidden |

To start with, a call is the Ready check sound and far away is the quiet Map ping, so the two can be told apart by ear.

**Resizing by dragging.** Three windows have a small grip in the bottom right corner. Hold the left mouse button on it and drag, like a window in Windows:

- **How is  doing**: becomes wider or taller, and the text re-wraps to fit.
- **The small DadMode window** and **the guide bar**: the whole window grows or shrinks, buttons and text together. The top left corner stays where it is.
- **The guide bar has a break point.** Drag it narrow and the buttons jump into one column. Drag it wide again and they go back to two. That is the same choice as **Guide bar layout** in the settings.

The size is remembered. The guide bar cannot be resized during a fight. **Window size** in the settings still works and applies on top, to everything at once. **Reset window sizes** in the settings, or `/dadmode resetsize`, puts it all back.

During a fight the game does not let an addon open the options window, so the shortcuts open the small DadMode window with the settings folded out instead.

To change who you follow, type `/dadmode`.

## What happens by itself

Kept deliberately short, so dad is not pestered.

| When | What dad sees |
|---|---|
| First party ever, nobody picked | The picker window opens. Once in a lifetime |
| Later parties where nobody is picked | One line in chat, at most every 10 minutes |
| A picked person is in the party | Arrows, and the green follow button |
| He drifts far away, same zone | One soft sound and one text each time |
| He is far away in another zone | Nothing. A grey arrow with the zone name |
| Someone calls or sends a marker | Sound, big text, pulsing arrow |
| He arrives | A short green message |
| A guide asks how he is doing | Nothing. His addon answers silently |
| Login, reload, loading screens, new zones | Nothing |

Guides are never asked to pick anyone.

## Roles: being guided, or a guide

Each computer running DadMode is one of two things:

- **Being guided** ("dad"): sees calls, gets the far warning and the follow button, and answers when a guide asks how he is doing.
- **A guide**: gets the guide buttons. Calls, far warning and follow button are off, because a guide is not the one who gets lost.

**The role is asked once.** The first time DadMode starts on a computer, a small window asks **Who is using DadMode on this computer?** with two buttons: **I need help finding my party** and **I am a guide for someone**. After that it is never asked again: not at login, not on reload, not when entering a dungeon or a new zone. The answer is saved for the whole game account on that computer. A computer that already used an earlier DadMode is not asked at all and keeps the role it had.

To change role later, type `/dadmode role`. That reopens the same question. There is deliberately no role switch in the everyday window, so it cannot be flipped by accident.

**If calls end up switched off** for someone being guided, a red button **CALLS ARE OFF (click to fix)** appears in his window, and he gets a line in chat when someone calls him. One click repairs it. The caller sees **calls are off** on the guide bar.

## For the guides

Choose **I am a guide for someone** when DadMode asks at first start (or type `/dadmode role`). A compact bar with nine buttons appears. Drag it where you want it. The small **-** in its corner folds it up to just the title and the call status, and **+** opens it again. **Guide bar layout** in the settings switches between two columns and one narrow column.

Four buttons do two things each. Rest the mouse on a button to see what it does.

| Button | What it does |
|---|---|
| Call  | Beep and big text on his screen, and your arrow pulses white until he reaches you. While a call is running the button is red and reads **Cancel my call**: click it to take the call back |
| Come to me / Stop, wait here / Follow me | Same as a call, with that message |
| Waypoint for  | Puts a marker on dad's map and makes the game track it for him. See below. Once he has it, the button is red and reads **Remove the waypoint**. A right click always removes it |
| Star on my head | **Left click** puts a target marker on you, so he can see which character is you. **Right click** switches to the next icon. Give each guide a different one |
| Beam on the ground | **Left click**, then click the ground: a coloured beam marks the spot. **Right click** removes the beam |
| How is  doing | Opens a window with dad's status and his quests. See below |
| Quest list | Shows the small list that follows their quests, or puts it away. See "Doing a quest or a dungeon together" |

To see what dad sees when he is called, use **Test a call** in the settings, or `/dadmode test`.

**The strip at the bottom of the bar.** When you are guiding somebody, the bottom of the guide bar shows two lines about him, by itself:

- **Who and where**: his name, level, zone, and how many yards away he is.
- **What needs attention**, or **all good** in green when nothing does:

| Shows | When |
|---|---|
| **DEAD** (red) | He is dead |
| **bags full** (red), or **2 bag slots left** (orange) | 2 free slots or fewer |
| **2 broken** (red) | Broken gear |
| **gear 18%** (orange) | His most worn piece is under 25%, before it breaks |
| **no food** (orange) | No food or drink in his bags |
| **1 talent point** (orange) | Unspent talent points |
| **has DadMode 1.27.0, you have 1.30.0** | His version is not the same as yours |

With several people to guide and "everyone" chosen, each gets one line. With nobody to guide the strip is gone and the bar is shorter. The bar only changes size outside a fight.

Somebody who is not in your party but answered a moment ago is shown too, with **not in your party** in place of the distance.

When no call is running, what matters most is also on the top line, so it shows with the bar folded up. The guide's addon asks for this short status every 45 seconds. Dad needs DadMode 1.19 or newer to answer; with an older version it only updates while **How is  doing** is open.

**Version check.** The same area says when someone in the party runs another DadMode than you: "Dad has DadMode 1.14.2, you have 1.19.0". Most "it does not work" moments so far came from that. Addons tell each other their version when the party changes.

**A new version is out.** An addon can not look on the internet. But when somebody in your party runs a newer DadMode than you, yours says so once: **DadMode 1.30.0 is out. You have 1.29.0. Update it in the CurseForge app.** The one being guided also gets it as the big text on the screen, since he may not read chat.

### What would this item change for him?

No need to inspect him. The guide's addon knows what he wears and shows what would change. **It states facts and gives no verdict.** Whether Strength or Spell Power is better depends on how he plays, and that is for you to judge.

**In every item tooltip** (loot window, roll window, chat links, bags, vendors) a guide gets extra lines:

- **Dad wears [Old Cloth Hood] item level 31**
- **This one: item level 38 (+7)**
- **gains +4 Intellect, +6 Stamina** in green
- **loses -3 Spirit** in red

Other cases: **Dad has nothing in that slot**, **Dad wears this**, **Dad can not wear plate**, **This is leather. He can wear mail**, **Needs level 42, he is 38**. For rings, trinkets and one-hand weapons it compares against the one of his two with the lower item level.

**When gear drops** (roll window, your own loot window, or the party's loot line in chat) you get one chat line: **Dad can wear [Drowned Crown] item level 38. He wears [Old Cloth Hood] item level 31. +4 Intellect, +6 Stamina, -3 Spirit.** For every green or better item that he can wear in his own armor type and does not already wear.

It does not know which weapon types he has trained. The armor rules are the classic ones: cloth for priest, mage and warlock; leather for rogue and druid; hunter and shaman move from leather to mail at 40; warrior and paladin from mail to plate at 40.

His gear is fetched by itself when you group up and again every ten minutes. His class and level are read straight from the game on the guide's side, so the armor check works whatever version he has. He needs DadMode 1.8 or newer for the comparison at all, and 1.15 or newer for exact items with enchants. **Compare drops with their gear** in the settings turns it off.

### Gear in his bags, and "put it on"

The **Gear** tab starts with **In his bags**: one row for each thing in his bags that he could wear. Every row is laid out the same way:

| Left | Middle | Right |
|---|---|---|
| The slot: Head, Ring, Main hand | The item and its item level. Under it, what it would replace. Under that, small chips: green for what he gains, red for what he loses | A button |

- Hold the mouse over either item name for the game's own tooltip.
- An item for an empty slot says **his main hand slot is empty**.
- Lighter armor says so: **this is leather, he can wear mail**.
- What he can put on now comes first. Then items that need a higher level, the same item he already wears, and last what he can not wear (**Dad can not wear plate**). Those have no button.

**What counts for him.** Above the rows is a line of small buttons, one for each stat that shows up in the list: Strength, Agility, Spell Power and so on. Click the stats that matter for how he plays. From then on:

- Items that gain those stats come first, the biggest gain on top. Items that lose them sink below the rest.
- The chips for his stats are bright and come first on each row. The other chips are dimmed.

The addon does not guess this. You tell it, once, and it is remembered for that person. Click a stat again to switch it off.

**Sort.** Under that line: **By slot**, **Item level** (the biggest step up in item level first, an empty slot counts in full), and **His stats** (only there when you have picked some). Picking a stat switches to His stats by itself.

**The button.** Click **Put it on** and on his screen a call sounds, the text says **Anna says: put on Mail Coif**, and a big gold button appears: **CLICK TO PUT ON: Mail Coif**. One click and the item goes on. Your button shows what happened:

| Button | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Put it on (gold) | Click to ask him |
| Asked (grey) | Sent, no answer yet |
| He sees it (grey) | The gold button is on his screen |
| He put it on (green) | Done |
| Didn't work (red) | He clicked but the item did not go on. He has to right-click it in his bags |
| Not in bags (red) | He no longer has it |
| Not sent (red) | The message could not be sent. Chat says why |

Any button except the green one can be clicked again.

- During a fight his button says to click again afterwards. The game does not allow changing armor in a fight.
- The gold button on his screen goes away by itself after two minutes.

His addon sends up to 16 wearable things from his bags. He needs DadMode 1.21 or newer for all of this.

**Who you are guiding.** The buttons carry the name of the one they are for: **Call Olaf**, **Waypoint for Olaf**, **How is Olaf doing**. A line at the top of the bar says **Guiding: Olaf**.

With two or more people to guide in the party, that line reads **Guiding: everyone (click to change)**. Click it to go through them one by one. With one person chosen, calls, cancels and waypoints go only to that person; with **everyone**, to all of them. A person you aim at needs DadMode 1.23 or newer; an older version gets the message the old way, to everybody.

Anyone in the party who runs DadMode and is not a guide counts as someone to guide.

**Being approved.** The one you guide has to say yes to you once. Until then your window says ** has not approved you as a guide yet** and a call shows ** has not approved you** on the bar. When he clicks Yes you get a chat line and the window fills by itself. If he has switched something off, the tab says so plainly: ** does not share his gear with guides**.

### Waypoint for 

Press **Waypoint for ** and two things happen on his screen:

- A **red, pulsing arrow** labelled **MARKER** appears next to his other arrows, pointing at the spot, with the distance. This is the part he will notice.
- The game's own pin is set on his world map and minimap and tracked.

He gets the call sound and the text ** put a marker on your map. Follow the red arrow**. When he gets within 15 yards the marker removes itself, he sees **You reached the marker**, and your chat says he arrived. He can also remove it with **Remove the red marker** in his picker window.

The pin on the map itself keeps the game's own look. Addons cannot recolour it, which is why the red arrow carries the signal.

Which spot is sent:

- If you have set **your own map pin** (the game's map pin on the world map), that spot is sent. So to send him anywhere: put your own pin there first, then press the button.
- Otherwise, **the spot where you are standing**.

Your chat tells you which one was used, and then whether dad's addon managed to set it. It replaces any pin dad had set himself. It does not work in dungeons, and the red arrow needs him to be on the same continent as the spot. Otherwise it says to open the map.

### When the waypoint is far away: zeppelins and flight points

If the marker is on another continent, or so far away that a zeppelin is clearly shorter, dad's addon gives him the trip in steps:

1. Big text: **Take the zeppelin to Grom'gol. Go up the tower at Orgrimmar, north side. Zeppelin master Snurk Bucksquick stands on the right platform.**
2. The red arrow is labelled **ZEPPELIN** and points to that exact platform, with the distance.
3. On the platform it says **Right platform. Wait here for the zeppelin to Grom'gol.**
4. When he lands, it says **Now follow the red arrow** and the arrow points to the marker again.

If he takes the wrong zeppelin, the addon sees where he landed and gives the next step from there.

**At a flight master.** When he opens the flight map while he has a marker, big text says **Fly to: **: the flight point he can fly to that is closest to where he has to go. It only shows when flying gets him clearly closer.

Zeppelins it knows (Horde): Orgrimmar to Undercity, Orgrimmar to Grom'gol, Undercity to Grom'gol, each in both directions.

Boats it knows: Ratchet to Booty Bay, Steamwheedle Port to Powderfuse Port, Zephras Isle to Skywatcher Plateau, each in both directions. For a boat the text is **Take the boat to Booty Bay. It leaves from the dock at Ratchet**, the arrow says **BOAT**, and on the dock it says **Right dock. Wait here**.

**Where the dock spots come from.** No site publishes exact dock positions for Forever, and nobody that Questie knows stands on a dock.

- **Ratchet and Booty Bay** work from the start, roughly: the arrow leads to the town (the flight master's spot, from the wowforever.be flight path guide), and then it says **You are in Ratchet. Go to the dock and wait for the boat to Booty Bay.**
- **Steamwheedle Port, Powderfuse Port, Zephras Isle and Skywatcher Plateau** have no published spot at all. Those routes are not suggested until a guide has recorded both ends.

To record an exact spot, a guide stands on the dock and types `/dadmode stop NAME`. `/dadmode stop` alone lists the names, such as `BB_RATCHET` for the Booty Bay dock where the boat to Ratchet leaves. A spot recorded by hand is sent along with the next waypoint and replaces a rough or looked-up one on dad's side, so the same command also fixes a zeppelin platform that points to the wrong place. `/dadmode travel` shows for each stop whether it is known, rough, recorded by a guide, or unknown.

**Where the platform spots come from.** A zeppelin master stands on every platform, and Questie knows where they stand. A computer with Questie looks them up by itself. When a guide sends a waypoint, the spots are sent along, so dad does not need Questie. `/dadmode travel` lists which platforms this computer knows.

Limits: the arrow cannot point up, so climbing the tower is text only. An addon cannot see which zeppelin is docked or when it leaves. Which side of the tower is taken from the classic game; if Forever differs, go by the zeppelin master's name.

### Doing a quest or a dungeon together

For "we are doing this right now" there is a small list on the guide's screen, like the game's own quest tracker, but with **his** progress:

```
Olaf's quests
Bloodscalp Ears        6/15   you 9/15
The Idol               0/1
Into the Deep          ready to hand in
```

It follows along by itself: when he loots something for a quest, the number changes a moment later. Nothing to refresh.

**What is on it, without you choosing anything**

| Where you are | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Out in the world | Every quest both of you have, his progress next to yours |
| In a dungeon | His quests for that dungeon, and nothing else. The heading says **Olaf in Zul'Farrak** |

**A quest of his that you do not have.** Open the **Quests** tab and click **Track** on its row. It stays on the list until you click **Stop following**. Quests you share say **Followed**.

**While you play**

- When he finishes a quest on the list, chat says **Olaf finished Bloodscalp Ears. Hand in: Kin'weelay, Stranglethorn Vale.**
- When you are done with a quest and he is not, his numbers turn orange, so you do not run off.
- Hold the mouse over a line for his objectives, yours, and where it is handed in. Click it to open that quest in the window.
- At most six lines. Drag the list to move it.
- **The Quest list button on the guide bar** shows the list and puts it away. Shown with the button, it stays on the screen also when there is nothing to follow, and says how it fills. The **x** on the list puts it away too.
- Left alone, the list comes by itself when there is something to follow, and is not there otherwise.

**Before a dungeon.** Pick the dungeon on the **Dungeon** tab. Above the quests it says **Ready to go in?** with his gear, bag space and food, and says **repair first** when his gear is worn. Under that are the dungeon's quests he has not picked up, with who gives them. Inside it is too late for both.

**Coming out.** Chat says what he still needs: **Olaf still needs from Zul'Farrak: Scarab Shells (3/5)**.

**In a dungeon the game can hold messages back**, in fights for certain and maybe the whole time. His addon keeps trying, so the list catches up as soon as the game allows. When its numbers are more than a minute and a half old it says so: **from 3 min ago**.

He needs DadMode 1.32 or newer for the list to follow along by itself. The dungeon part needs Questie on the guide's computer.

### His talents

The **Talents** tab draws his talent trees the way his own talent window shows them: every talent is a picture in the same row and column, with its rank under it (**3/5**). Taken talents are bright, the rest are dimmed. The name of each tree has its points next to it, so **Enhancement 31** tells you his build at a glance, and with that which stats to click under **What counts for him** on the Gear tab.

- The line at the top says how many points he has to spend.
- Hold the mouse over a talent for its name, rank and where it sits.
- **Click a talent to point at it.** On his screen a call sounds and the big text says **Anna says: put your talent point in Flurry**, with the tree and the row, counted from the top. Your tab says **Told him**, then **He sees it**. He spends the point himself; the game does not let anybody do that for him.
- **Right click a talent to take it back.** Clicked the wrong one, or changed your mind: the pointing goes away on your tab, and his screen says **Anna took that back. Do not spend the point yet.** Then point at another one.

Nothing is written per class. His addon reads whatever trees his character has and sends them, so it works for every class and keeps working when the game changes its talents.

WoW Forever keeps all talents of a class in one big tree with three named groups; the addon reads that (1.33). The older way, where the game has three separate trees, is read too, so the same addon works on both kinds of game version.

His talents are only asked for when you open this tab, and again with Refresh. He needs DadMode 1.31 or newer. If his game version does not let an addon read talents, the tab says so.

### When he is not in your party

You can still see how he is doing. Your addon remembers everybody you have guided: that happens by itself the first time you open the window in a party with them. After that, opening the window when he is not in your party asks him directly. Nothing shows in chat on either side.

| What you see | Meaning |
|---|---|
| The usual tabs, with **Olaf is not in your party. This is how he is doing right now.** | He is online and answered |
| **Olaf is not online.** | The game said so. He is not asked again for two minutes |
| **Olaf does not answer.** | He is online but his addon stays quiet: he has DadMode older than 1.28, or he has not approved you |

- **Put it on**, and his talents with pointing at one, work outside the party too.
- Arrows, distance, the far-away warning, calls and waypoints need a party. The game only tells positions inside one.
- He needs DadMode 1.28 or newer, and so do you.
- `/dadmode forget olaf` takes somebody off your list.

### The "How is  doing" window

The top line says who it is about: **Olaf  Shaman, level 40, Stranglethorn Vale**. It is the same on every tab. With more than one person to guide it says **How are they doing** and each name is on the page.

The window has six tabs:

| Tab | Shows |
|---|---|
| **Overview** | A grid of small boxes with his status, how many quests he has and how many are ready to hand in, and how many of your quests he is missing |
| **Quests** | His quest list, one row for each quest, with search |
| **Missing** | Your quests that are not in his log: not picked up, or already done. With search |
| **Dungeon** | Every quest for one dungeon, and where he stands on each. See below |
| **Gear** | What is in his bags against what he wears, his total stats, what he wears, and his potions, food and bandages |
| **Talents** | His talent trees, drawn like his own talent window. See below |

Colours mean the same thing everywhere: **gold** is a name or a heading, **green** is fine, done, or a gain, **orange** needs attention soon, **red** is urgent, missing, or a loss, and grey is less important. On the screen of the one being guided, the big text and the arrows use calmer shades of the same colours, so nothing glares at him.

Every list is built the same way: one row for each thing, a label on the left, the name, small coloured boxes for the state (green is good or done, red is missing or lost, grey is a plain fact), and a button on the right when there is something to do. The colours and the gold edge are the game's own, and every DadMode window and button has them: the guide bar, the window to pick people, the Yes / No box, the follow button.

The Overview tab's boxes:

- **Level**, with how far to the next level, and his **Gold**.
- **Right now**: DEAD, in a fight, or away from keyboard, when that applies.
- **Where**: zone and area. Works across zones, where the arrow gives up.
- **Looking at**: his target.
- **Bags**: free slots. Orange at 6 or fewer, red at 2 or fewer, FULL at 0.
- **Gear**: his most worn piece in percent, and how many pieces are broken. Orange at 40%, red at 20% or when something is broken.
- **Food and drink**, **Bandages** and **Potions** in his bags.
- **Hearthstone**: where it is set and whether it is ready.
- **Talent points**, when he has unspent ones and the game reports them.
- **Quests** and **Missing**.

The **Quests** tab: level, what is left to do, **ready to hand in** first, and **you have it too** on quests you share.

**Search.** On the Quests and Missing tabs, the box under the tabs filters the list while you type. It looks in quest names and objectives. The **x** clears it.

**Compare with your own quests.** Every quest of his is marked **you have it too** or **only **. When you share a quest, a blue line under his objectives shows your own progress. The **Missing** tab lists each of your quests that is not in his log:

- **not picked up** (red): he never took it, or abandoned it.
- **already done** (green): he has handed it in before.

Before a dungeon this shows at a glance which pickups he is missing, as long as one guide has all the quests. His game is the only one that knows what he has already done, so he needs DadMode 1.16 or newer for this list. With an older version it says so.

**Dungeon.** The **Dungeon** tab first lists the dungeons that have quests. The one he is standing in comes first. Click **Open**. You then get every quest Questie knows for that dungeon, each with his state:

- **in his log** (green), with his progress, or **ready to hand in**
- **not picked up** (red), with **starts at:** who gives it and where, and **needs level N** when he is too low
- **already done** (grey)

Three boxes at the top count them: In his log, Not picked up, Already done. This catches quests that none of you has picked up, which the Missing tab cannot. **Other dungeon** goes back to the list. The search box works here too.

It needs Questie on the guide's computer; dad does not need it. Dad needs DadMode 1.16 or newer to answer which quests he has already done. The list is Questie's list for your own race and class, so a quest only dad's class can do is not in it, and a quest that needs an earlier quest first still shows as not picked up.

**Gear.** The **Gear** tab shows what he is wearing: every slot with the item's name in its quality colour and its item level, plus the average item level. An empty armour or weapon slot shows **EMPTY** in red. Worn pieces show their condition, and **BROKEN** at zero. **Show quests** swaps back. Works at any distance, unlike the game's own Inspect. Under the gear it lists **which** potions, food and drink, and bandages he carries, with how many of each.

**Item stats.** In the gear list, hold the mouse over an item name and the game's own tooltip appears, with all its stats. If dad has DadMode 1.15 or newer it is the exact item he wears, with enchants and random stats. With an older version on his side it is the plain item.

**Total stats.** Above the gear list there is a **Stats** block: health, mana, armor, stamina, intellect, spirit, strength, agility, spell power, healing, spell crit, attack power and melee crit. A value the game does not give to addons is left out. Dad needs DadMode 1.15 or newer for this block.

**Where to hand in.** If the guide has the Questie addon installed, each quest that is ready shows **hand in: , **, so the list doubles as a route.

**Follow-up quests.** With Questie, each quest also shows **then: ** when it is part of a chain. The game does not provide this, Questie's database does, so it only appears on a computer with Questie. Quests Questie does not know simply show no "then" line.

The window refreshes by itself once a minute while it is open, and shows how old the information is. Refresh asks right away. It does not refresh while a list is still coming in or while you are typing in the search box.

**Long quest lists.** The game only lets an addon send a short burst of messages and then about one a second. Anything sent faster is thrown away without a warning. Before 1.18 that cut long quest lists short: the header stayed on "loading..." and some quests never showed. From 1.18 his addon sends at the pace the game allows, quests first, so a full log of about 30 quests takes roughly 10 seconds and the header counts up ("loading 12 of 29"). During a refresh the old list stays on screen and the new one replaces it when it is complete. If he is on an older version and the end of the list is lost, the window shows what arrived and says "only 12 of 29 arrived".

Turning the guide bar on also turns pings, far warnings and the follow button off for you, since you are not the one who gets lost.

**The line at the top of the guide bar** shows what happened to your call: *Calling...*, then * got it  85 yd* with his distance counting down as he walks to you, then * is with you*. *No answer* in red means nobody replied.

After a call you also get two lines in chat: ** got your call** when his addon received it, and ** is with you** when he arrives.

If nothing comes back within 3 seconds you see **Nobody answered**: nobody else in the party has DadMode running. If the other person has calls switched off (guides do), you are told that instead. You never see your own calls.

No addon? Type `!dad` or `!dad come here` in party chat. Dad's addon reacts to that too. `!dad ok` cancels it.

### Built in so nobody gets annoyed

- One sound at a time, never two within 2 seconds.
- A second call from the same person within 3 seconds is ignored.
- The call ends by itself when he is within 12 yards of the caller.
- No far warning while someone is calling him. One thing at a time.
- The far-away sound plays once each time he drifts off, not on repeat. There is no repeat, and none at all when that person is in another zone. Dad can switch the whole warning off in the picker window.
- Dad picks his own sounds, including no sound at all.

## Minimap button

A gold arrow button on the edge of the minimap.

- **Left click**: the window for your role. For dad that is **Who do you want to find?**, where he picks who to find and follow. For a guide it shows or hides the guide bar with the commands (not during a fight). **How is  doing** is a button on that bar.
- **Right click**: the DadMode page in the game options.
- **Drag** it around the minimap to move it.
- `/dadmode minimap` hides it or brings it back.

If another addon has installed the usual minimap button library (LibDBIcon), DadMode uses it, so button collectors such as MinimapButtonButton pick it up like any other addon. Otherwise it draws its own button.

## Which version am I on

The guide bar tells you by itself when someone in the party has another version than you.

**Everyone's version.** The bottom of the **Overview** tab in **How is  doing** lists every person in the party with role and version: "Ben: guide, DadMode 1.20.1, same as yours", "Dad: being guided, DadMode 1.14.2, older than yours", or "no DadMode seen". `/dadmode status` prints the same list in chat. The role is shown for people on 1.20.1 or newer; for older versions it says "role unknown", or "being guided" once that person has answered a status request. Next to a name it also says **answers only to you**, or that his answers go to the whole party because sending them to you alone does not work.

The version is shown in the top right corner of the **Who do you want to find?** window, next to the title of the **DadMode guide** bar, and by `/dadmode status`. When dad's addon answers a call, the guide's chat line also shows dad's version.

## Commands

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `/dadmode` | Open the window to pick people. It also has Move arrows and the far warning switch |
| `/dadmode settings` | Open the DadMode page in the game options |
| `/dadmode resetsize` | Put every window back to its normal size |
| `/dadmode testbox` | Show the Yes / No box with a made-up guide, to look at it alone |
| `/dadmode guides` | Open the My guides page, and list guides and permissions in chat |
| `/dadmode role` | Reopen the question: being guided, or a guide |
| `/dadmode on`, `/dadmode off` | Show or hide the arrows |
| `/dadmode minimap` | Show or hide the minimap button |
| `/dadmode alerts` | Turn incoming pings on or off |
| `/dadmode follow` | Show or hide the green follow button |
| `/dadmode test` | Show on your own screen what dad sees when called |
| `/dadmode stop NAME` | Record the dock or platform you stand on. Without a name it lists the names |
| `/dadmode travel` | List the zeppelin platforms this computer knows, and the route to the current marker |
| `/dadmode waypoint` | Send dad a waypoint: your map pin if you have one, otherwise where you stand |
| `/dadmode quests` | Open the "How is  doing" window |
| `/dadmode tracker` | Guides: show the small quest list or put it away, same as the Quest list button |
| `/dadmode forget NAME` | Guides: stop asking this person how he is doing when he is not in your party |
| `/dadmode debug` | Print the names the game reports and what the last incoming call looked like. For troubleshooting |
| `/dadmode status` | Show your role, whether you show calls, and who is in the party |
| `/dadmode clear` | Remove the ping on screen right away |
| `/dad` or `/dad some text` | Send a ping to the party |

## Privacy

His status, quests, gear and bag contents (level, gold, location, target, bag space, what he wears and its condition, consumables, hearthstone, and quests) go only to a guide he has approved, and only what he shares under **My guides**. They are sent to that one guide alone, so no other computer receives them. Nothing is sent unless a guide asks.

A guide outside his party can ask too, but only one he has already said yes to. Anybody else who asks from outside his party gets no answer, and no Yes / No box appears.

## Limits

- **Arrows work outdoors only.** Inside dungeons the game does not tell addons where players are, so no addon can point a direction there. What dad gets in a dungeon instead: under each picked name it says **close by** (green) or **TOO FAR AWAY** (red), which is the game's own 40 yard check. If even that is not available he sees "no arrows in here". Calls, the follow button, the marker over your head and the ground beam all still work in dungeons.
- In a dungeon there is no far-away sound. The game lets the addon show the too-far text but not read it.
- **Addons cannot draw in the 3D world.** They cannot highlight a character or paint the ground. The marker over the head and the ground beam are game features, which is why they are buttons you press and not automatic.
- Pings sent with the addon can be blocked by the game during boss fights. `!dad` in party chat is the fallback.
- The guide buttons and the follow button cannot be shown, hidden, moved or changed during a fight. That is a game rule for buttons that act for you. The follow button still works in a fight, it just keeps pointing at the same person until the fight ends.
- Follow is the game's own `/follow`. It needs the person to be nearby and in view.
- **A guide cannot make dad's character follow by remote.** The game only lets a character start following from that player's own click or key press. The closest possible is what the addon does: the guide presses Follow me, and dad's green button switches to the guide and flashes until he clicks it.
- Distances are in yards, as the game measures them.

## How it works, for whoever maintains it

- Positions: `UnitPosition(unit)` for the player and each party member, with `C_Map.GetPlayerMapPosition` plus `C_Map.GetWorldPosFromMapPos` as a fallback. Arrow angle = `atan2(west difference, north difference) - GetPlayerFacing()`.
- Pings: addon messages with prefix `DADMODE` sent to `PARTY`. `PING:<text>` calls, `CLEAR` cancels, `ACK`, `HERE` and `MUTED` are the replies to the guide. Party chat and whispers starting with `!dad` trigger the same alert. Pings from people outside the party are ignored.
- Names: Forever characters have a first name and a surname ("Anna Stormhoof"). The game gives the first name in some places and the full name, sometimes with realm, in others. Everything is matched on the first name in lower case (`Key()`). Before 1.3.2 calls were silently dropped because of this.
- The follow button is a `SecureActionButtonTemplate` button running the macro `/follow party1` (the unit, not the name).
- Gear comparison: `Compare(link, d)` reads the slot from `C_Item.GetItemInfoInstant`, the level from `C_Item.GetDetailedItemLevelInfo`, and the difference from `C_Item.GetItemStats`. Tooltips are hooked with `TooltipDataProcessor.AddTooltipPostCall(Enum.TooltipDataType.Item, ...)`, or `OnTooltipSetItem` on older clients.   | File | Job |
  |---|---|
  | `Core.lua` | Constants, small helpers, who is in the party, where everybody is, the big message |
  | `Messages.lua` | Sending to the party or to one person at the pace the game allows. The list of every message type is at the top of this file |
  | `UI.lua` | Buttons, backgrounds, text size, resize corners |
  | `Travel.lua` | Zeppelin and boat steps, flight point hint |
  | `Arrows.lua` | The arrows to picked people and to the marker |
  | `Calls.lua` | Calls: sending, showing, answering |
  | `Picker.lua` | The "Who do you want to find?" window |
  | `GuideBar.lua` | The guide's bar and the role question |
  | `Waypoints.lua` | Waypoints from a guide |
  | `Report.lua` | What the one being guided reports: status, quests, gear, bags |
  | `Window.lua` | The "How is  doing" window |
  | `Rows.lua` | The page inside that window: text, rows (label, facts, chips, button), lines of small switches, and grids of boxes |
  | `Follow.lua` | The green follow button |
  | `Frames.lua` | The arrow bar, the big message frame, the timer that drives everything |
  | `Minimap.lua` | The minimap button |
  | `Options.lua` | The settings page |
  | `Events.lua` | Game events and incoming messages |
  | `Slash.lua` | `/dadmode` and `/dad` |
  | `Dungeon.lua` | The Dungeon tab |
  | `Compare.lua` | Gear comparison, gear in bags, put-it-on |
  | `Target.lua` | Who a guide's calls are for |
  | `Guides.lua` | Approval and permissions |
  | `Extras.lua` | Version check, warnings on the guide bar, polling |
  | `Private.lua` | The guide's safety net for whispers |
  | `Remote.lua` | Guiding somebody who is not in the party, by whisper |
  | `Talents.lua` | His talents: reading them, sending them, pointing at one |
  | `Tracker.lua` | The small quest list that follows his progress, and telling the guides when a quest changes |
